title: Convergent prefix hashing and compact-rewrite for cross-request KV reuse
creator: Aarti Mehta
description: Problem: Our current prefix caching stores request-aligned prompt fragments which leads to high duplication in GPU-resident KV storage for semantically identical prefixes that differ only in punctuation, whitespace, or template slots. This increases GPU memory pressure and reduces hit rates for inter-request reuse, driving up per-token cost and tail latency during compaction.
proposal: Introduce a convergent prefix canonicalization pipeline + compact-rewrite stage before cache fingerprinting. Steps: 1) Apply lightweight normalization (unicode NFC, whitespace collapse, punctuation normalization, stable slot markers). 2) Run a short, deterministic sketch (64-bit stable hash with seed per-model-family) and a Bloom filter pre-check to group likely-similar prefixes. 3) For grouped candidates, compute an edit-aware canonical form by trimming repeated tokens, normalizing stop/close tokens, and optionally substituting common templates with canonical placeholders. 4) Create a compact rewrite token sequence (lossless index map to original tokens) and store/lookup against the cache using the convergent hash. 5) On hit, reconstruct or patch the KV entries into the request’s slot mapping with minimal copy semantics and update residency credits for eviction heuristics.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end testbench shows >=12% improvement in cross-request prefix hit rate on internal conversational workload suite. 2) Median generation latency change <= +2ms on P99-critical paths. 3) GPU-resident KV footprint reduction of >=8% at 95th percentile under mixed-tenant traffic. 4) No user-visible output regressions on curated eval set (BLEU/ROUGE/QA exact match thresholds). 5) Rollout togglable per-model and with telemetry to revert quickly.
metrics: prefix_hit_rate_target: +12% relative, kv_gpu_bytes_95p_reduction_target: 8%, p95_inference_latency_delta_target: <=+25ms absolute, cost_per_token_reduction_estimate: 6%
implementation_notes:
- Implementation will add a new canonicalization stage in request pre-processing and a compact-rewrite encoder that emits a short mapping table (stored off-GPU in compressed metadata; only compacted KV tensors live on GPU).
- Hashing: use xxh3 seeded per-model-family for speed; fall back to full canonical compare for collisions.
- Store canonical fingerprint and original fingerprint; support dual-lookup during rollout window.
- Compact rewrites should include an index patch so we can apply KV slices without full tensor copy when shapes align.
- Eviction: increment residency credit of merged entries to avoid premature eviction; introduce micro-slab reclaim job that runs during low utilization windows to defragment GPU slabs.
- Back-compat: feature gated by model/route and circuit-breaker flag; safe-fallback path always present to use original fingerprinting if canonicalization fails.
- Observability: add tag canonicalized=true/false on cache events; log transform ratio and collision counts.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Internal testbench and canary on internal staging (1 node) with simulated traffic (2 weeks). Stage 2: Select small percentage of production traffic for read-only canonical lookups (no write) to measure hit-rate delta (2 weeks). Stage 3: Enable writes for non-critical model families (10% traffic) and monitor. Stage 4: Gradual ramp to 100% per-model after meeting safety metrics. Each stage bounded by automatic rollback if GPU memory regression > +5% or token-level quality regressions detected.
risks:
- Over-normalization may change model outputs for templates with semantically-significant punctuation.
- Hash collisions could cause incorrect KV reuse if canonical compare path is faulty.
- Additional CPU work in pre-processing may increase request queuing on high QPS routes.
- Complexity of reconstructing KV slices without copying may introduce subtle GPU memory leaks.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for normalization and canonical forms for a wide set of templates and languages.
- Property tests: round-trip compact-rewrite -> reconstruct -> encode produces identical generation outputs for target prompts.
- Load test with mixed tenant trace replay to validate p95 latency and memory behavior.
- A/B quality evals against our regression suite and human spot-checks on edge cases.
- Fuzzing for hash collision scenarios and corrupted mapping tables.
notes:
Spike completed (2025-05-20) demonstrating 15% hit-rate improvement on internal e2e replay for support-conversations. Initial microbench shows CPU preproc adds ~0.6ms median on dedicated worker threads but can be batched. Next: prototype patch to runtime kernel to support zero-copy KV patching.
